source.title: Some open problems about the solutions of the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/\sqrt{x_{n-1}}

accepted.question_text: Consider the nonlinear delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/\sqrt{x_{n-1}} for n=0,1,2,\ldots with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-1} and x_0. When 0<A<15/4, is the unique positive equilibrium \bar{x} of this equation globally asymptotically stable?
accepted.context_brief: Global stability for the square-root delay equation when 0<A<15/4.

evidence.quote: Let \bar{x} denote the unique positive equilibrium of Eq. (1). (a) Show that when 0<A<15/4 the positive equilibrium of Eq. (1) is globally asymptotically stable.

accepted.question_text: Consider the nonlinear delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/\sqrt{x_{n-1}} for n=0,1,2,\ldots with arbitrary positive initial values x_{-1} and x_0. When A>15/4, does this equation possess an asymptotically stable periodic orbit of prime period two?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotically stable 2-cycle for the square-root delay equation when A>15/4.

evidence.quote: (b) Show that when A>15/4 there exists a periodic cycle with period two which is asymptotically stable.

accepted.question_text: For the recurrence x_{n+1}=a/x_n^2+1/x_{n-1} for n=0,1,2,\ldots, for which values of the parameter a is the unique positive equilibrium \bar{x} globally asymptotically stable?
accepted.context_brief: Global stability range for the equilibrium of Eq. (16).

evidence.quote: Open problem 1. (a) For what values of a is the positive equilibrium \bar{x} of Eq. (16) globally asymptotically stable?

accepted.question_text: For the recurrence x_{n+1}=a/x_n^2+1/x_{n-1} for n=0,1,2,\ldots, when Eq. (16) has the period-two cycle {p,q,p,q,\ldots} with p=(a+\sqrt{a^2+2-2\sqrt{1+4a^2}})/2 and q=(a-\sqrt{a^2+2-2\sqrt{1+4a^2}})/2, for which values of a is this period-two cycle asymptotically stable, and what is its basin of attraction?
accepted.context_brief: Stability and basin of attraction of the explicit 2-cycle of Eq. (16).

evidence.quote: Open problem 1. (b) For what values of a is the periodic cycle {p,q,p,q,\ldots} of Eq. (16) asymptotically stable? What is its basin of attraction?

accepted.question_text: Consider the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p for n=0,1,2,\ldots. What conditions on the parameters A, p, and k guarantee that the positive equilibrium of this equation is globally asymptotically stable?
accepted.context_brief: Global stability conditions for the general delayed family in Eq. (19).

evidence.quote: Open problem 2. (a) Obtain conditions on A, p and k under which the positive equilibrium of Eq. (19) is globally asymptotically stable.

accepted.question_text: Consider the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p for n=0,1,2,\ldots. What conditions on the parameters A, p, and k ensure that this equation has periodic cycles of period two; under what conditions are those period-two cycles stable; and what are their basins of attraction?
accepted.context_brief: Existence, stability, and basins of 2-cycles for Eq. (19).

evidence.quote: Open problem 2. (b) Obtain conditions on A, p and k under which Eq. (19) has periodic cycles of period two. Under what conditions on A, p and k are these periodic cycles stable? What is the basin of attraction?

accepted.question_text: Consider the delay difference equation x_{n+1}=A/x_n^2+1/x_{n-k}^p for n=0,1,2,\ldots. Can this equation have periodic cycles whose prime period is greater than two?
accepted.context_brief: Higher-period cycles for the general delayed family in Eq. (19).

evidence.quote: Open problem 2. (c) Do there exist periodic cycles of period greater than two?
